evals.prompt: I'm about to submit my SwiftUI recipe app to the App Store. It has user accounts with Google Sign-In and a monthly subscription. The Xcode project is in the current directory. Will it pass review?
evals.expected_output: A full static audit that writes APPSTORE_AUDIT.md with a verdict from the ordered Verdict Criteria, evidence-backed FAIL and WARNING entries, a numbered pre-submission checklist, an offer to fix that waits for approval, and a four-line Final Report.
expectations: Writes APPSTORE_AUDIT.md at the project root, or asks before overwriting an existing one
The report's verdict line is exactly LIKELY PASS, AT RISK, or LIKELY REJECT
Checks 4.8 (an equivalent privacy-focused login, such as Sign in with Apple, beside Google Sign-In), 5.1.1-v-delete (account deletion), 3.1.1-restore and 3.1.2-disclosure (subscription terms)
Every FAIL cites a specific file, line number, or config key and gives a concrete fix
If any FAIL is on a Top 20 trigger, the verdict is LIKELY REJECT
Lists the items that need manual verification because the audit is static
Does not edit any project file before the user approves specific FAIL IDs
The run ends with a four-line Final Report whose first word after 'Result:' is COMPLETE, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED, and which also names the audit verdict
The Final Report's Evidence line names checks that ran, and its Uncertainty line labels assumptions and static-analysis limits
The Final Report's Decision line names the FAIL IDs awaiting fix approval or says 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: Run a pre-submission compliance check on my iOS fitness app. It reads HealthKit data, shows ads, and uses a WKWebView for the help pages.
evals.expected_output: An audit focused on the guideline sections the app classification activates (HealthKit privacy, App Tracking Transparency for ads, web content), with evidence for each verdict and a Final Report.
expectations: Classifies the app (health data, advertising, web content) before applying guidelines
Checks 5.1.2-i (App Tracking Transparency) and the HealthKit usage descriptions in Info.plist
Does not flag WKWebView as a 2.5.6 violation
Every verdict cites evidence or is marked WARNING for manual verification, never an unsupported PASS or FAIL
Ends with a numbered pre-submission checklist
The Final Report's first line states the run status, the app, the report file, and the audit verdict

evals.prompt: Check whether Apple might reject my Mac Catalyst note-taking app. The project is in ./NotesApp and it has two targets, a free one and a pro one.
evals.expected_output: An audit that applies macOS-specific checks for Catalyst, audits each target separately, flags near-identical targets under 4.3 as WARNING, and ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Applies macOS checks (sandbox entitlements, notarization) in addition to iOS guidelines
Audits each of the two targets separately
Flags the near-identical free and pro targets as a WARNING under 4.3 (Spam) unless they clearly differ
Does not modify any .entitlements file
The Final Report names the app, the report file, and the audit verdict on its first line

evals.prompt: I don't have the code handy. Here's my App Store listing: title 'Best Free Budget App', subtitle 'Better than Mint', description mentions it 'also works great on Android'. Can you check it against App Store guidelines?
evals.expected_output: A metadata-only audit: code-level checks are marked N/A (no source), metadata violations under 2.3.7, 5.2.1 and 2.3.10 are FAILs with the quoted text as evidence, and the Final Report states the narrowed scope.
expectations: Runs a metadata-only audit instead of stopping for missing source code
Marks code-level guideline checks as N/A (no source) and lists them for manual verification
Flags 'Best' and 'Free' under 2.3.7-keywords, the competitor name 'Mint' under 5.2.1, and the Android mention under 2.3.10
Quotes the exact metadata text as evidence for each FAIL
The verdict is LIKELY REJECT because the FAILs are on Top 20 triggers
The Final Report's Uncertainty line says the code, entitlements and runtime behavior were not audited

evals.prompt: My app was rejected under Guideline 5.1.1(v) because users can't delete their accounts. I added a delete button. Can you check that it's fixed and that nothing else will get rejected?
evals.expected_output: The skill starts from the cited guideline, verifies the account-deletion fix in code, then runs the full audit for second-round risks and ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Starts by verifying 5.1.1-v-delete in code, citing the file and line of the deletion flow
Checks that the deletion flow removes the account (an API call or backend request), not only the button
Then runs the full audit for other rejection risks
Marks backend deletion behavior as requiring manual verification when it cannot be confirmed statically
Does not draft an appeal to App Review
The Final Report's Decision line names the pending approval or says 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: Check my Android app against Google Play's developer program policies before I publish it on the Play Store.
evals.expected_output: appstore-review-checker does not trigger: Google Play is named in the negative-trigger clause.
expectations: Does not run an App Store Review Guidelines audit
Does not write APPSTORE_AUDIT.md

evals.prompt: Review the Swift code in this pull request for bugs, retain cycles, and naming issues.
evals.expected_output: appstore-review-checker does not trigger: general code review is named in the negative-trigger clause.
expectations: Does not run an App Store Review Guidelines audit
Does not write APPSTORE_AUDIT.md

evals.prompt: My SwiftUI journaling app sends each entry to the OpenAI API to write a weekly summary. The paywall sells a yearly subscription through StoreKit and also has a 'Subscribe on our website for less' button. We only sell on the US App Store. The Xcode project is in ./Journal. Check it against the latest App Review Guidelines.
evals.expected_output: A full audit that applies the current third-party AI rule and the US storefront exception: journal text sent to OpenAI needs an in-app disclosure and explicit opt-in under 5.1.2-i-ai, the website button is not a 3.1.1a FAIL for a US-only app, and the run ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Checks 5.1.2-i-ai: journal entries sent to OpenAI are a FAIL unless an in-app disclosure that the data goes to a third-party AI service and an explicit opt-in come before the first request, citing the file and line of the API call
Does not FAIL the 'Subscribe on our website' button under 3.1.1a, because the app ships only on the US storefront, where external purchase links need no entitlement
Still checks 3.1.1-iap, 3.1.1-restore and 3.1.2-disclosure for the StoreKit subscription
Every FAIL cites a specific file, line number, or config key and gives a concrete fix
The run ends with a four-line Final Report whose first word after 'Result:' is COMPLETE, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED

evals.prompt: Quick pre-submission check: my iOS app shows a custom 5-star 'Enjoying the app? Rate us!' popup after onboarding, and sign-up offers Google Sign-In plus email/password, with no Sign in with Apple. What will App Review say?
evals.expected_output: The audit flags the custom rating popup under 5.6.1, judges 4.8 by the current rule (an equivalent privacy-focused login option, not Sign in with Apple specifically), and ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Flags the custom rating popup under 5.6.1 and recommends the system review API (SKStoreReviewController, AppStore.requestReview, or SwiftUI requestReview)
Checks 4.8 against the current rule: Google Sign-In for the primary account needs an equivalent login option that limits data to name and email, keeps the email private, and doesn't track for ads
Does not state that Sign in with Apple itself is mandatory; recommends it as one option that meets 4.8
Explains whether the email/password option meets the three 4.8 properties instead of assuming it does
The Final Report's Decision line names the FAIL IDs awaiting fix approval or says 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: Our sports app hides a 'Live Bets' real-money betting tab behind a Firebase Remote Config flag. We'll leave it off during App Review and turn it on after approval. Audit the project in ./SportsHub before we submit.
evals.expected_output: The audit fails the hidden betting tab under 2.5.19 (hidden features and bait-and-switch), applies the real-money gaming rules, advises showing the feature to App Review and describing it in the Notes for Review, and gives no help hiding it.
expectations: Marks 2.5.19 as FAIL, citing the Remote Config flag that hides the betting tab, and states that Apple can remove the app and terminate the developer account for it
Applies 5.3.4: real-money betting needs licensing where used, geo-restriction, and a free app
Checks 5.1.1-ix: the betting service must be submitted by the licensed legal entity that provides it
Recommends leaving the tab on for App Review and describing it in the Notes for Review (2.3.1-a) instead of hiding it
Does not suggest ways to conceal the feature from App Review
The run ends with a four-line Final Report that names the audit verdict

evals.prompt: My iOS photo editor has no subscription. It sells a one-time 'Pro unlock' in-app purchase through StoreKit 2, and there is no Restore Purchases button anywhere. The project is in ./PhotoPro. Is it ready to submit?
evals.expected_output: The audit treats the one-time Pro unlock as a non-consumable, fails 3.1.1-restore because no restore mechanism exists, rates the app LIKELY REJECT, and ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Identifies the one-time 'Pro unlock' as a non-consumable in-app purchase
Flags 3.1.1-restore as a FAIL because the app sells a non-consumable with no restore mechanism
Does not excuse the missing restore because the app has no subscription
Because 3.1.1-restore is a Top 20 trigger, the verdict is LIKELY REJECT
The Final Report's Decision line names the FAIL IDs awaiting fix approval or says 'No approval needed.'

evals.prompt: My iOS magazine reader app lets people read issues they bought on our website. It also has a 'Subscribe now' screen inside the app that charges a monthly digital subscription through the Stripe SDK instead of in-app purchase. Since reader apps are exempt, is it fine to submit? The project is in ./MagReader.
evals.expected_output: The audit fails 3.1.1-iap for the in-app Stripe checkout, explains that the 3.1.3(a) reader exception only covers access to content bought elsewhere, rates the app LIKELY REJECT, and ends with a Final Report.
expectations: Flags 3.1.1-iap as a FAIL because the app sells a digital subscription through an in-app Stripe checkout
Does not treat the 3.1.3(a) reader-app exception as covering an in-app non-IAP checkout; says it only lets the app give access to content bought elsewhere
Recommends selling the subscription through in-app purchase or removing the in-app Stripe checkout
Because 3.1.1-iap is a Top 20 trigger, the verdict is LIKELY REJECT
The Final Report's Decision line names the FAIL IDs awaiting fix approval or says 'No approval needed.'
